value.body: Many design graduates work independently — for agencies, startups, brands or individuals — on graphics, UI/UX, product, fashion or interiors. A freelance practice means finding your own clients, pricing projects, managing contracts and paperwork, and handling uneven income.

items.label: Entry requirement
items.note: Clients judge you mainly on your portfolio

items.label: GST registration
items.note: For service providers; ₹10 lakh in special category states; registration needed earlier for some cases

items.label: Business registration
items.note: Free and online; optional but useful for some schemes and clients

items.label: B.Des students enrolled
items.note: All years of the B.Des programme, all modes; design degrees recorded under other names are not included

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A strong portfolio and a few first clients — often from internships, former employers, referrals or freelance platforms. Many designers work in a studio or agency for a year or two first to learn client handling and process.

value.title: At a glance
items: Income is irregular; saving a buffer for slow months is common practice.
Written agreements typically cover scope, number of revisions, payment schedule and who owns the final files and rights.
Pricing per project rather than per hour is common, and late payments are a frequent problem.

value.title: B.Des enrolment in India
value.note: Counts students across all years of the B.Des programme, not new admissions or freelance designers. Based on institutions that reported to AISHE; specialised design degrees with other names are counted separately.
